newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW shares surge 9.9 pct in early trade.
newsitem.headline: VW shares surge 9.9 pct in early trade.

text.p: Shares in German carmaker Volkswagen AG, which on Thursday jumped through the important 1,000 mark ($581) barrier, surged again on Friday morning on the back of its positive business outlook for the 1997 year.

Volkswagen shares were trading 104 marks or 9.9 percent higher at 1,150 in IBIS computer trading at about 0657 GMT, below a high of 1,194.95 hit soon after trade started. By 0703 GMT the share had eased slightly to 1,135.30 in active trading.
Volkswagen on Thursday kicked off 1997 by predicting better first quarter results due to a 9.5 percent rise in sales, adding it expected higher profits and sales for the year.
The company's 1996 results got a hefty lift from the German mark's decline in currency markets.

VW said in its 1996 annual report that it expected "positive results" for 1997 despite forecasts for slow consumer spending as many European nations slash spending to qualify for European currency union set to begin in 1999.
Its 1996 results were hurt by a 1.5 billion mark ($870 million) charge to reduce the interest rate growth forecast for its pension funds to five percent from six percent.
If VW had not opted for the pension fund change, VW officials said the results would have been sharply above the doubling in 1996 group profit of 678 million marks.
